title: add benchmark-lab representative workload runners and reporting pipeline v29
author: Priya Shah
description: This PR adds a new set of representative workload runners for the benchmark lab, updates profiling baselines for cold-start and steady-state runs, and wires results into the reporting pipeline (v29). Motivation: recent model-architecture and kernel-selection changes changed sequence-length latency distributions; we need updated representative runners and updated profiling baselines so the reporting pipeline produces accurate cost/latency regressions. Changes include new runner configs, small runtime adapters to stabilize KV cache priming, metrics instrumentation additions, and reporting pipeline transformations to normalize sample metadata. Checklist: - [x] add representative workload runners for convo, instruction, and embedding workloads - [x] update profiling baselines (cold-start and steady-state) for 1k/4k token workloads - [x] add metrics (per-batch token distribution, cache-hit-rate) to runner telemetry - [x] add transformation step in reporting pipeline to annotate runs with kernel selection profile - [x] update docs/quickstarts referencing new runner configuration example - [x] CI green and performance smoke tests pass Notes: kept changes isolated and backwards compatible with existing runner interfaces; reporting transformation is additive and gated behind a feature flag for rollout.
commits: perf(profiling): update cold-start and steady-state baselines for 1k/4k seq lengths
chore(ci): add smoke test job for benchmark-lab runners
feat(reporting): add kernel-profile annotation transform and normalize metadata
fix(runtime): stabilize KV priming path for deterministic cache-hit-rate in tests
docs: update benchmark-lab quickstart and runner examples

+++ b/benchmark-lab/runners/representative/conversation_runner.py
@@ -12,6 +12,14 @@
 def run_conversation(batch):
-    # existing logic

+    if config.get("force_kv_priming"):
